result: In 128 post-COVID patients followed 2-12 months, objective cognitive impairment (GDS>0.5) ranged 16-26% (46.5% impaired at least once) and blood kynurenine pathway metabolites were associated with cognitive impairment and PASC.
reason: Blood KP metabolites measured in a long COVID cohort; LC version of the pathway finding, but no controls and the abstract gives no direction or effect size.

result: A systematic review of 101 studies found no validated ME/CFS diagnostic biomarker; 79% of candidates were blood-based, and reproducibility across studies was limited.
reason: A narrative review of biomarker candidates; it does not test the sampling-coverage claim (rest vs PEM window, severity, compartments).

result: In 710 patients 6-11 months after hospital discharge for COVID-19, 36.1% reported slightly worse and 14.6% severely worse cognition; cognition was tied to sociodemographic factors, with no prominent role for acute severity or inflammatory markers.
reason: Hospitalised post-COVID cohort with self-reported change and no domain-level deficit comparison against controls; not the ME/CFS cognitive-domain profile, and no atlas finding covers it.

result: In 77 long COVID patients vs 766 non-COVID patients with undifferentiated dyspnea, percent-predicted peak VO2 was lower (73 vs 85%); ventilatory inefficiency was similar (19% in both groups), and marked limitation was uncommon.
reason: Independent cohort, same CPET measure and same direction; the comparison group was dyspneic non-COVID patients rather than recovered controls.

result: In 83 adolescent ME/CFS patients, extracranial Doppler CBF fell 27% at 20-degree tilt vs 31% at 70-degree tilt (p=0.003); no POTS at 20 degrees vs 32% at 70 degrees.
reason: Same measure, but no healthy controls; it adds an adolescent subgroup and a tilt-angle comparison rather than replicating the case-control difference.

result: In 83 adolescent ME/CFS patients, extracranial Doppler CBF fell 27% at 20-degree tilt vs 31% at 70-degree tilt (p=0.003); no POTS at 20 degrees vs 32% at 70 degrees.

result: In long COVID patients who improved after two cycles of therapeutic apheresis, neurotransmitter autoantibodies, lipids and inflammatory markers fell, and fibrinogen fell 70%.
reason: Does not compare autoantibody levels with controls or test whether they are elevated; the treatment aspect is covered by the immune-immunoadsorption link.

result: In long COVID patients who improved after two cycles of therapeutic apheresis, neurotransmitter autoantibodies, lipids and inflammatory markers fell, fibrinogen fell 70%, and rouleaux and fibrin fibres largely disappeared on dark-field microscopy.
reason: Another uncontrolled open-label apheresis report consistent with the open-label clause; adds lipid and fibrinogen markers; weak design with no sham and no responder vs non-responder comparison.

result: In 362 ME/CFS patients without POTS or hypotension vs 52 controls, end-tilt stroke volume index was lower (22 vs 27 ml/m2), with heart-rate rises below the control prediction interval (orthostatic chronotropic incompetence).
reason: Same Doppler SVI-on-tilt measure; adds the incomplete compensatory heart-rate response in normal-HR/BP patients; van Campen 2023 is not among the cited studies.

result: In 362 ME/CFS patients without POTS or hypotension vs 52 controls, end-tilt SVI was lower (22 vs 27 ml/m2), with an inadequate heart-rate increase for the SVI fall.
